title: local kv offsets & seqlen anomalies — scratch
observed_errors: MismatchError: KV cache write offset != expected_offset (got 37824, expected 37888)
TokenAlignmentException: token_id 50256 repeated at position 1023 after recompute
OOM avoided by fallback but produced length-truncation (approx -1 tokens)
Trace log: kvcache.set(key=layer3, offset=0x930) then kvcache.get(key=layer3, offset=0x918)
hypotheses: Edge-case sequence lengths (just above page/chunk boundary, e.g., 1024/1536) cause kernel selector to choose a generic kernel that writes KV with a different alignment (8 vs 16 byte), producing an off-by-1-timestep offset.
Quantized kernels (int8 path) use a packed layout for keys/values; packing alignment change + prefetching leads to mis-index when prefix caching is active.

Race between async KV flush and attention compute when using continuous batching: older requests flushes KV for shorter seqlen, next request expects last_write_offset == current_offset but gets stale offset due to reorder.
A protective fallback introduced in PR #1423 (kernel mux) didn't update legacy KV writer offsets; regression introduced for tensor shapes > 1536.
Inconsistent pad/truncate logic in preprocess -> runtime input slicing leads to off-by-pad in stamp stored in kvcache metadata (pad_count vs true_length).
reproduction_steps: 1) Start local runtime with kvcache tracing: ./run_infer.sh --trace kvcache --kvcache-mode local
2) Send two requests back-to-back: first seq_len=768 (warm), then seq_len=1025 (edge) with same conversation_id param to hit prefix cache path.
3) Observe traces in /tmp/runtime-traces: grep 'kvcache' | less -> look for inconsistent offsets or repeated keys.
4) Run regression build: git bisect between v2025.09 and main to isolate commit that first changes KernelSelector thresholds.
5) Reproduce with quantized vs fp16 model variants to see if int8 path differs.
6) If reproduced, attach full trace and run small patch that forces KernelSelector to pick old kernel: export FORCE_KERNEL=fast_attn_v1 and re-run.
7) Capture memmaps: export KV_DEBUG_DUMP=/tmp/kvdump && reproduce -> inspect binary offsets using hexdump -C kvdump_layer3.bin
notes:
Timeline + informal log:

2025-11-04 initial discovery: noticed a customer report about 'stutter' when sending chat messages that crossed 1024 tokens. Repro locally with redwood-v2-small: observed token repeat at boundary.

2025-11-05 ran quick bisect: suspected kernel selector thresholds. Put an initial workaround: force kernel selection to fast_attn_v1 = reduces failures but increases latency.

2026-01-14 after release 2026.01.11, recurrence in dedicated capacity with larger batches. Now see fallbacks to generic_attn but also OOM-avoided truncation. Traces show kvcache writes being performed with different offsets depending on kernel path.

Trace snippet (sanitized):
  [kvcache] set layer=3 offset=0x930 len=16384 ts=1700003452 request_id=abc123
  [attn] kernel=fast_attn_v2 seq_len=1536 choose=heuristic(seq_len>1280)->v2
  [kvcache] get layer=3 offset=0x918 len=16384 ts=1700003452 request_id=def456
  --> mismatch (0x930 vs 0x918)

Immediate theory: writer alignment changed from 0x8 stepping to 0x10 stepping when v2 kernels pack KV differently. read path still expects old stepping.

Other notes:
- Observed that using conversation_id isolation (per-request cache key) mitigates the issue; suggests collision/reuse rather than pure math bug.
- Repro is flaky: ~60% on CPU debug builds, ~95% on optimized quantized builds on A100. Flakiness suggests timing/race.
- Adding a short sleep (0.01s) between warm request and edge request reduces incidence. Points to race between async KV flush and next request read.

Files to attach to ticket: full runtime trace, hexdump of kvdump, kernel selection logs, small repro script.

Open questions to triage:
- Does KernelSelector.describe() have an up-to-date mapping for quantized models? (Samir to check mapping table)
- Is there any code path that updates kvcache metadata asynchronously without atomically swapping base_offset?
- Are we using the same packer/unpacker across all kernel codepaths?

Short-term mitigation ideas:
- Add a runtime assertion in kvcache.get that compares caller_expected_alignment vs stored_alignment and fails fast (debug only).
- Force kernel selector to a single codepath for sequences in [1024, 1600] as a canary for customers (config flag).
- Add a lightweight spin-wait for outstanding kvcache flushes when prefix cache is enabled (trade latency for correctness).

End of scratch.
